parts.name: casting

physics.Basic_description: The main body of the plane, a heavy black cast iron casting with a flat sole and raised sides.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural backbone and weight necessary for smoothing wood surfaces.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the central body firmly from the sides or top to support the tool's weight.
physics.reason: Cast iron plane bodies are thick-walled shells with internal voids to save material while maintaining rigidity, not solid blocks.

parts.description: The main body of the plane, a heavy black cast iron casting with a flat sole and raised sides.
parts.function: Provides the structural backbone and weight necessary for smoothing wood surfaces.

parts.name: sole edge

physics.Basic_description: The bottom surface edge of the plane body, appearing as a thin strip in side view, machined flat.
physics.Functional_description: The reference surface that rides on the workpiece to ensure a flat cut.
physics.Grasped_description: Not intended for grasping; this is the contact surface with the workpiece.
physics.reason: The sole is a thick, machined section of the casting treated as solid material for physics purposes.

parts.description: The bottom surface edge of the plane body, appearing as a thin strip in side view, machined flat.
parts.function: The reference surface that rides on the workpiece to ensure a flat cut.

parts.name: frog

physics.Basic_description: An angled black metal platform mounted on the body bed, supporting the blade assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Holds the cutting iron at the correct angle and allows for mouth adjustment.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and recessed to grasp independently; handled via the main body.
physics.reason: The frog is a dense, block-like cast iron component with minimal internal voids relative to its size.

parts.description: An angled black metal platform mounted on the body bed, supporting the blade assembly.
parts.function: Holds the cutting iron at the correct angle and allows for mouth adjustment.

parts.name: depth stud

physics.Basic_description: A small threaded steel rod or stud visible near the depth adjustment mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Part of the linkage connecting the depth wheel to the blade assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp; manipulated indirectly via the depth wheel.
physics.reason: Small mechanical fasteners and studs are solid metal rods.

parts.description: A small threaded steel rod or stud visible near the depth adjustment mechanism.
parts.function: Part of the linkage connecting the depth wheel to the blade assembly.

parts.name: cap screw

physics.Basic_description: A small metallic screw head securing the lever cap.
physics.Functional_description: Clamps the lever cap down onto the cutting iron.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small for gripper manipulation; requires a tool or fine motor skill.
physics.reason: Screws are solid metal components.

parts.description: A small metallic screw head securing the lever cap.
parts.function: Clamps the lever cap down onto the cutting iron.

parts.name: iron

physics.Basic_description: A flat, silver-colored steel blade with a sharpened edge, angled upwards.
physics.Functional_description: The actual cutting tool that removes shavings from the wood.
physics.Grasped_description: Sharp and dangerous to grasp directly; handled by the body or knobs.
physics.reason: Plane blades are solid plates of hardened steel.

parts.description: A flat, silver-colored steel blade with a sharpened edge, angled upwards.
parts.function: The actual cutting tool that removes shavings from the wood.

parts.name: cap

physics.Basic_description: A gold/brass-colored metal plate sitting on top of the blade assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Presses the cutting iron firmly against the frog to prevent chatter.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to lift the assembly, but usually manipulated via the cam lever.
physics.reason: Lever caps are thick, solid castings designed to withstand high clamping force.

parts.description: A gold/brass-colored metal plate sitting on top of the blade assembly.
parts.function: Presses the cutting iron firmly against the frog to prevent chatter.

parts.name: knob

physics.Basic_description: A turned, reddish-brown wooden knob located at the front of the plane.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a handhold for the user to guide and press down on the front of the plane.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the knob from above or the side to steer the plane.
physics.reason: Wooden knobs are turned from solid stock.

parts.description: A turned, reddish-brown wooden knob located at the front of the plane.
parts.function: Provides a handhold for the user to guide and press down on the front of the plane.

parts.name: tote

physics.Basic_description: A curved, reddish-brown wooden handle rising from the rear of the plane.
physics.Functional_description: The primary handle for the user to push and control the plane.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the handle firmly with a power grip to apply forward force.
physics.reason: Wooden handles are solid carved components.

parts.description: A curved, reddish-brown wooden handle rising from the rear of the plane.
parts.function: The primary handle for the user to push and control the plane.

parts.name: lever

physics.Basic_description: A thin metal lever protruding from the top of the blade assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Adjusts the lateral tilt of the blade to ensure an even cut across the width.
physics.Grasped_description: Pinch the lever tip to shift it left or right.
physics.reason: Thin levers are solid metal strips.

parts.description: A thin metal lever protruding from the top of the blade assembly.
parts.function: Adjusts the lateral tilt of the blade to ensure an even cut across the width.

parts.name: wheel

physics.Basic_description: A knurled brass-colored wheel located behind the frog.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated to raise or lower the cutting depth of the blade.
physics.Grasped_description: Pinch the wheel edges and rotate to adjust depth.
physics.reason: Adjustment wheels are typically solid or thick-walled castings treated as solid for mass estimation.

parts.description: A knurled brass-colored wheel located behind the frog.
parts.function: Rotated to raise or lower the cutting depth of the blade.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
